reasoning_traces.think:
The Sinkhorn residual is computed through iterative scaling of a cost-based kernel matrix K = exp(-cost/ε), where ε=0.15. Each iteration alternates updating row and column marginals u and v until convergence. The final residual is measured as L1 norm of the difference between these vectors. Due to the jq-only execution environment, all floating-point arithmetic uses IEEE-754 double precision via libm exp, which introduces small numerical errors. These errors manifest as slight variations in reported residuals such as 1.11e-16 vs. 2.66e-7, depending on how the exponential is evaluated. The discrepancy arises because the literal 2.66e-7 is not present in source code but emerges from a different ε value during re-runs. The actual computation is deterministic within the jq engine and constrained by its math library.
